# TypeSpec assessment end-to-end evidence

This directory is the repeatable regression suite for the 11 historical
TypeSpec assessments. It separates inputs, accepted outputs, generated outputs,
and legacy evidence:

- `cases.json` is the authoritative case and workspace manifest. Each entry
  records the PR, exact base/head commits, TypeSpec projects, and expected
  conclusion counts.
- `assessments/<pr>/` contains the accepted `assessment.json` and final
  `assessment.html`. These files are committed regression oracles.
- `outputs/<pr>/` is generated by the runner and is intentionally ignored.
  Each run retains `assessment.json`, `assessment.html`, and `result.json`.
- `.workspaces/<pr>/` is generated and ignored. Sparse pilot cases contain a
  blob-filtered bare object store plus explicit detached `base` and `head`
  workspaces at the manifest commits.
- `fixtures/` and the historical finalization scripts preserve lower-level
  curated evidence used by focused unit tests and report reconstruction.

## Replay all accepted assessments

From the repository root:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-e2e.mjs
```

Run one case or choose a persistent output location:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-e2e.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --output C:\temp\typespec-assessment-e2e
```

The replay validates the assessment schema, verifies exact base/head commits and
expected conclusion counts, renders HTML with the current renderer, and rejects
canonical HTML drift. Because the runner writes outside Vally's temporary
workspace when `--output` is absolute, the HTML remains available after Vally
finishes.

## Replay versus the full sparse pilot

`run-e2e.mjs` is a deterministic **replay** of committed accepted assessments.
It validates existing JSON and rerenders HTML, but it does not fetch source,
compile TypeSpec, produce fresh model input, or perform fresh Agent judgment.

Each historical case's **full sparse E2E run** starts from exact remote Git objects,
materializes sparse base/head source, runs deterministic assessment analysis,
and prepares a bounded work item for the parent Agent. The coordinator does not
invoke an LLM and does not claim full end-to-end completion. Full completion
requires the parent Agent to review the fresh `model-input.json`, write the
judgment artifacts, assemble the assessment, and validate the final report.

## Materialize historical sparse workspaces

The pilot requires an explicit case. From the repository root, use the default
`https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs.git` remote:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\materialize-workspaces.mjs `
  --case 44988
```

For a local or hermetic Git remote override:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\materialize-workspaces.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --repository C:\workspace\azure-rest-api-specs `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\.workspaces
```

The case directory contains `source.git`, `base`, `head`, and
`materialization-manifest.json`. Initialization and depth-limited fetches use
`blob:none`, no tags, and the PR ref when available. Commit/tree history is
deepened only until Git can resolve the base/head merge base; unrelated service
blobs remain excluded. Both workspaces use cone sparse checkout with
`cases.json` `sparseRoots`. Reuse verifies the remote, promisor filter, commits,
clean worktrees, and sparse metadata; unexpected directories are never
replaced. The materializer also verifies that root
`package.json` and `package-lock.json` blobs are identical at base and head, so
toolchain setup cannot enter the assessed diff, and records both paths and blob
IDs in the materialization manifest. Materialization does not require or link
dependencies.

## Run the deterministic Network pilot

Run all deterministic phases and prepare the Agent handoff:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988
```

By default, the `dependencySetup` phase copies the historical head
`package.json` and `package-lock.json` into
`outputs\network-pilot\44988\cache\toolchain`, runs `npm ci` there once, and
junctions or symlinks that single `node_modules` into both historical
workspaces. It reruns installation only when the cache is absent or fails the
unchanged core preflight. The links are ignored setup and do not alter the
tracked TypeSpec diff.

The runner uses a bounded 300 KiB model-input budget because the largest case's 16
changed source files and documentation/source review pairs exceed the core
250 KiB default. Override it with `--model-input-budget-bytes <bytes>` when
measuring a different bound; the selected value is recorded in
`pilot-manifest.json`.

Use a local source remote, explicit caches, or resume a completed phase:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --repository C:\workspace\azure-rest-api-specs `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988 `
  --document-cache $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988\cache\documents `
  --artifact-cache $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988\cache\artifacts `
  --checkout-cache $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988\cache\checkouts `
  --resume
```

An existing authoring-fixture installation can be reused only when it matches
the selected PR's historical lockfile:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --node-modules C:\workspace\azure-rest-api-specs\node_modules `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988
```

A mismatched override fails preflight instead of falling back to installation.
`--phase materialize`, `--phase dependency-setup`, `--phase analyze`, and
`--phase prepare-agent` run one stage when its prerequisites already exist.
Analyze requires a successful `dependencySetup`; `--phase all` is the default
and stops at the Agent boundary.
`pilot-manifest.json`, `pilot-summary.json`, and `agent-work-item.json` are
machine-readable and resumable. A successful deterministic run ends with
`status: "awaiting-agent-judgment"` and leaves the fresh model input under
`deterministic-analysis\model-input.json`.

`prepare-agent` records when the handoff becomes ready, but does not start the
judgment timer. As its first action after it is actually scheduled, the assigned
Agent must mark its execution start:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --phase start-agent `
  --workspace-output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\.workspaces `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988
```

This separates `agentQueueMs` from `agentJudgmentMs`. For latency benchmarks,
run one Agent case at a time. Parallel runs measure suite throughput; their
queue times must not be interpreted as per-case judgment latency.

After the assessment skill writes fresh `assessment-judgment.json` and
`materialization-assessment.json`, finish the measured E2E run with:

```powershell
node .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.mjs `
  --case 44988 `
  --phase finalize `
  --workspace-output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\.workspaces `
  --output $PWD\.github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\outputs\network-pilot\44988
```

The finalizer computes Agent judgment time from the explicit Agent start, passes
the measured value to the existing assembler, validates the final JSON, and
records `agentQueueMs`, `agentJudgmentMs`, `skillE2eMs`, and
`timingQuality: "measured"` in `pilot-summary.json`. `skillE2eMs` includes
deterministic analysis, active Agent
judgment, assembly, validation, and rendering. It excludes one-time historical
workspace and dependency setup as well as Agent scheduling queue time. Do not
substitute a model estimate for this measurement. Manifests produced before the
explicit start protocol remain readable, but their timing quality is
`queue-inclusive-legacy` rather than measured. Each measured report is retained under
`reports\<agent-start-epoch>[-<rerun>]\assessment.{json,html}`, so a later run
cannot overwrite an earlier measurement. Finalization restores complete
operation contracts and retained source evidence through the existing
assembler; that work is included in the measured E2E duration.

No core assessment flags or setup changes are required; the coordinator invokes
the existing `run-assessment-analysis.mjs` contract unchanged.

## Vally

The skill eval at `assessment.eval.yaml` covers routing boundaries and uses PR
44988 as the representative report-generation capability case. The deterministic
Node E2E test covers all 11 cases without model or network variability:

```powershell
node --test .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-e2e.test.mjs
node --test `
  .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\materialize-workspaces.test.mjs `
  .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment\evals\scripts\run-network-pilot.test.mjs
vally lint .github\skills\azure-typespec-assessment --strict
```
